objects.definition: typedef size_t csh;
objects.description: Opaque handle type used by all Capstone APIs. It is an alias of size_t and is passed by value to most APIs; some functions take a pointer to it to initialize or close the handle.

objects.definition:
typedef enum cs_arch {
	CS_ARCH_ARM = 0,	///< ARM architecture (including Thumb, Thumb-2)
	CS_ARCH_ARM64,		///< ARM-64, also called AArch64
	CS_ARCH_MIPS,		///< Mips architecture
	CS_ARCH_X86,		///< X86 architecture (including x86 & x86-64)
	CS_ARCH_PPC,		///< PowerPC architecture
	CS_ARCH_SPARC,		///< Sparc architecture
	CS_ARCH_SYSZ,		///< SystemZ architecture
	CS_ARCH_XCORE,		///< XCore architecture
	CS_ARCH_M68K,		///< 68K architecture
	CS_ARCH_TMS320C64X,	///< TMS320C64x architecture
	CS_ARCH_M680X,		///< 680X architecture
	CS_ARCH_EVM,		///< Ethereum architecture
	CS_ARCH_MOS65XX,	///< MOS65XX architecture (including MOS6502)
	CS_ARCH_WASM,		///< WebAssembly architecture
	CS_ARCH_BPF,		///< Berkeley Packet Filter architecture (including eBPF)
	CS_ARCH_RISCV,          ///< RISCV architecture
	CS_ARCH_SH,             ///< SH architecture
	CS_ARCH_TRICORE,	///< TriCore architecture
	CS_ARCH_MAX,
	CS_ARCH_ALL = 0xFFFF, // All architectures - for cs_support()
} cs_arch;
objects.description: Enumeration of architecture kinds supported by Capstone. Used with cs_open and cs_support.

objects.definition:
typedef enum cs_mode {
	CS_MODE_LITTLE_ENDIAN = 0,	///< little-endian mode (default mode)
	CS_MODE_ARM = 0,	///< 32-bit ARM
	CS_MODE_16 = 1 << 1,	///< 16-bit mode (X86)
	CS_MODE_32 = 1 << 2,	///< 32-bit mode (X86)
	CS_MODE_64 = 1 << 3,	///< 64-bit mode (X86, PPC)
	CS_MODE_THUMB = 1 << 4,	///< ARM's Thumb mode, including Thumb-2
	CS_MODE_MCLASS = 1 << 5,	///< ARM's Cortex-M series
	CS_MODE_V8 = 1 << 6,	///< ARMv8 A32 encodings for ARM
	CS_MODE_MICRO = 1 << 4, ///< MicroMips mode (MIPS)
	CS_MODE_MIPS3 = 1 << 5, ///< Mips III ISA
	CS_MODE_MIPS32R6 = 1 << 6, ///< Mips32r6 ISA
	CS_MODE_MIPS2 = 1 << 7, ///< Mips II ISA
	CS_MODE_V9 = 1 << 4, ///< SparcV9 mode (Sparc)
	CS_MODE_QPX = 1 << 4, ///< Quad Processing eXtensions mode (PPC)
	CS_MODE_SPE = 1 << 5, ///< Signal Processing Engine mode (PPC)
	CS_MODE_BOOKE = 1 << 6, ///< Book-E mode (PPC)
	CS_MODE_PS = 1 << 7, ///< Paired-singles mode (PPC)
	CS_MODE_M68K_000 = 1 << 1, ///< M68K 68000 mode
	CS_MODE_M68K_010 = 1 << 2, ///< M68K 68010 mode
	CS_MODE_M68K_020 = 1 << 3, ///< M68K 68020 mode
	CS_MODE_M68K_030 = 1 << 4, ///< M68K 68030 mode
	CS_MODE_M68K_040 = 1 << 5, ///< M68K 68040 mode
	CS_MODE_M68K_060 = 1 << 6, ///< M68K 68060 mode
	CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN = 1U << 31,	///< big-endian mode
	CS_MODE_MIPS32 = CS_MODE_32,	///< Mips32 ISA (Mips)
	CS_MODE_MIPS64 = CS_MODE_64,	///< Mips64 ISA (Mips)
	CS_MODE_M680X_6301 = 1 << 1, ///< M680X Hitachi 6301,6303 mode
	CS_MODE_M680X_6309 = 1 << 2, ///< M680X Hitachi 6309 mode
	CS_MODE_M680X_6800 = 1 << 3, ///< M680X Motorola 6800,6802 mode
	CS_MODE_M680X_6801 = 1 << 4, ///< M680X Motorola 6801,6803 mode
	CS_MODE_M680X_6805 = 1 << 5, ///< M680X Motorola/Freescale 6805 mode
	CS_MODE_M680X_6808 = 1 << 6, ///< M680X Motorola/Freescale/NXP 68HC08 mode
	CS_MODE_M680X_6809 = 1 << 7, ///< M680X Motorola 6809 mode
	CS_MODE_M680X_6811 = 1 << 8, ///< M680X Motorola/Freescale/NXP 68HC11 mode
	CS_MODE_M680X_CPU12 = 1 << 9, ///< M680X Motorola/Freescale/NXP CPU12
				///< used on M68HC12/HCS12
	CS_MODE_M680X_HCS08 = 1 << 10, ///< M680X Freescale/NXP HCS08 mode
	CS_MODE_BPF_CLASSIC = 0,	///< Classic BPF mode (default)
	CS_MODE_BPF_EXTENDED = 1 << 0,	///< Extended BPF mode
	CS_MODE_RISCV32  = 1 << 0,        ///< RISCV RV32G
	CS_MODE_RISCV64  = 1 << 1,        ///< RISCV RV64G
	CS_MODE_RISCVC   = 1 << 2,        ///< RISCV compressed instructure mode
	CS_MODE_MOS65XX_6502 = 1 << 1, ///< MOS65XXX MOS 6502
	CS_MODE_MOS65XX_65C02 = 1 << 2, ///< MOS65XXX WDC 65c02
	CS_MODE_MOS65XX_W65C02 = 1 << 3, ///< MOS65XXX WDC W65c02
	CS_MODE_MOS65XX_65816 = 1 << 4, ///< MOS65XXX WDC 65816, 8-bit m/x
	CS_MODE_MOS65XX_65816_LONG_M = (1 << 5), ///< MOS65XXX WDC 65816, 16-bit m, 8-bit x
	CS_MODE_MOS65XX_65816_LONG_X = (1 << 6), ///< MOS65XXX WDC 65816, 8-bit m, 16-bit x
	CS_MODE_MOS65XX_65816_LONG_MX = CS_MODE_MOS65XX_65816_LONG_M | CS_MODE_MOS65XX_65816_LONG_X,
	CS_MODE_SH2 = 1 << 1,    ///< SH2
	CS_MODE_SH2A = 1 << 2,   ///< SH2A
	CS_MODE_SH3 = 1 << 3,    ///< SH3
	CS_MODE_SH4 = 1 << 4,    ///< SH4
	CS_MODE_SH4A = 1 << 5,   ///< SH4A
	CS_MODE_SHFPU = 1 << 6,  ///< w/ FPU
	CS_MODE_SHDSP = 1 << 7,  ///< w/ DSP
	CS_MODE_TRICORE_110 = 1 << 1, ///< Tricore 1.1
	CS_MODE_TRICORE_120 = 1 << 2, ///< Tricore 1.2
	CS_MODE_TRICORE_130 = 1 << 3, ///< Tricore 1.3
	CS_MODE_TRICORE_131 = 1 << 4, ///< Tricore 1.3.1
	CS_MODE_TRICORE_160 = 1 << 5, ///< Tricore 1.6
	CS_MODE_TRICORE_161 = 1 << 6, ///< Tricore 1.6.1
	CS_MODE_TRICORE_162 = 1 << 7, ///< Tricore 1.6.2
} cs_mode;
objects.description: Bitmask enumeration of architecture sub-modes and endianness, combined when opening a handle or changed via cs_option.

objects.definition: typedef void* (CAPSTONE_API *cs_malloc_t)(size_t size);

objects.definition: typedef void* (CAPSTONE_API *cs_calloc_t)(size_t nmemb, size_t size);
objects.description: Function pointer type for user-provided calloc replacement. Set in cs_opt_mem when configuring CS_OPT_MEM.

objects.definition: typedef void* (CAPSTONE_API *cs_realloc_t)(void *ptr, size_t size);
objects.description: Function pointer type for user-provided realloc replacement. Part of cs_opt_mem for CS_OPT_MEM option.

objects.definition: typedef void (CAPSTONE_API *cs_free_t)(void *ptr);
objects.description: Function pointer type for user-provided free replacement. Part of cs_opt_mem for CS_OPT_MEM option.

objects.definition: typedef int (CAPSTONE_API *cs_vsnprintf_t)(char *str, size_t size, const char *format, va_list ap);
objects.description: Function pointer type for user-provided vsnprintf replacement. Part of cs_opt_mem for CS_OPT_MEM option.
Container of user-defined memory management callbacks used by the engine when CS_OPT_MEM is set via cs_option. All fields optional; unspecified ones default to system allocators.
Customization record to override the mnemonic string of a specific instruction id. Used with cs_option(CS_OPT_MNEMONIC, ...).

objects.definition:
typedef enum cs_opt_type {
	CS_OPT_INVALID = 0,	///< No option specified
	CS_OPT_SYNTAX,	///< Assembly output syntax
	CS_OPT_DETAIL,	///< Break down instruction structure into details
	CS_OPT_MODE,	///< Change engine's mode at run-time
	CS_OPT_MEM,	///< User-defined dynamic memory related functions
	CS_OPT_SKIPDATA, ///< Skip data when disassembling. Then engine is in SKIPDATA mode.
	CS_OPT_SKIPDATA_SETUP, ///< Setup user-defined function for SKIPDATA option
	CS_OPT_MNEMONIC, ///< Customize instruction mnemonic
	CS_OPT_UNSIGNED, ///< print immediate operands in unsigned form
} cs_opt_type;
objects.description: Enumeration of runtime option categories accepted by cs_option.
Enumeration of option values used with cs_option for different cs_opt_type kinds.
Common operand types used across architectures when inspecting instruction details.
Bitmask enumeration of operand access (read/write) kinds for operands in instruction details.
Common instruction group identifiers used in cs_detail groups array and group name queries.

objects.definition: typedef size_t (CAPSTONE_API *cs_skipdata_cb_t)(const uint8_t *code, size_t code_size, size_t offset, void *user_data);
objects.description: Callback signature for SKIPDATA mode to decide how many bytes to skip at a given position.

User configuration for SKIPDATA mode: optional mnemonic string for skipped bytes, optional callback to determine skip length, and user_data passed to the callback. Provided to cs_option with CS_OPT_SKIPDATA_SETUP.

objects.definition:
typedef struct cs_detail {
	uint16_t regs_read[16]; ///< list of implicit registers read by this insn
	uint8_t regs_read_count; ///< number of implicit registers read by this insn

	uint16_t regs_write[20]; ///< list of implicit registers modified by this insn
	uint8_t regs_write_count; ///< number of implicit registers modified by this insn

	uint8_t groups[8]; ///< list of group this instruction belong to
	uint8_t groups_count; ///< number of groups this insn belongs to

	/// Architecture-specific instruction info
	union {
		cs_x86 x86;     ///< X86 architecture, including 16-bit, 32-bit & 64-bit mode
		cs_arm64 arm64; ///< ARM64 architecture (aka AArch64)
		cs_arm arm;     ///< ARM architecture (including Thumb/Thumb2)
		cs_m68k m68k;   ///< M68K architecture
		cs_mips mips;   ///< MIPS architecture
		cs_ppc ppc;	    ///< PowerPC architecture
		cs_sparc sparc; ///< Sparc architecture
		cs_sysz sysz;   ///< SystemZ architecture
		cs_xcore xcore; ///< XCore architecture
		cs_tms320c64x tms320c64x;  ///< TMS320C64x architecture
		cs_m680x m680x; ///< M680X architecture
		cs_evm evm;	    ///< Ethereum architecture
		cs_mos65xx mos65xx;	///< MOS65XX architecture (including MOS6502)
		cs_wasm wasm;	///< Web Assembly architecture
		cs_bpf bpf;	///< Berkeley Packet Filter architecture (including eBPF)
		cs_riscv riscv; ///< RISCV architecture
		cs_sh sh;        ///< SH architecture
		cs_tricore tricore; ///< TriCore architecture
	};
} cs_detail;
objects.description: Instruction detail structure populated when CS_OPT_DETAIL is ON and not in SKIPDATA mode. Provides implicit register reads/writes, group membership, and an architecture-specific union payload.
Top-level disassembled instruction record containing id, address, size, raw bytes, textual mnemonic and operands, and optional pointer to cs_detail when enabled.

objects.definition:
typedef enum cs_err {
	CS_ERR_OK = 0,   ///< No error: everything was fine
	CS_ERR_MEM,      ///< Out-Of-Memory error: cs_open(), cs_disasm(), cs_disasm_iter()
	CS_ERR_ARCH,     ///< Unsupported architecture: cs_open()
	CS_ERR_HANDLE,   ///< Invalid handle: cs_op_count(), cs_op_index()
	CS_ERR_CSH,      ///< Invalid csh argument: cs_close(), cs_errno(), cs_option()
	CS_ERR_MODE,     ///< Invalid/unsupported mode: cs_open()
	CS_ERR_OPTION,   ///< Invalid/unsupported option: cs_option()
	CS_ERR_DETAIL,   ///< Information is unavailable because detail option is OFF
	CS_ERR_MEMSETUP, ///< Dynamic memory management uninitialized (see CS_OPT_MEM)
	CS_ERR_VERSION,  ///< Unsupported version (bindings)
	CS_ERR_DIET,     ///< Access irrelevant data in "diet" engine
	CS_ERR_SKIPDATA, ///< Access irrelevant data for "data" instruction in SKIPDATA mode
	CS_ERR_X86_ATT,  ///< X86 AT&T syntax is unsupported (opt-out at compile time)
	CS_ERR_X86_INTEL, ///< X86 Intel syntax is unsupported (opt-out at compile time)
	CS_ERR_X86_MASM, ///< X86 Masm syntax is unsupported (opt-out at compile time)
} cs_err;
objects.description: Enumeration of Capstone API error codes returned by functions like cs_open, cs_disasm, cs_errno.

objects.definition: typedef uint16_t cs_regs[64];
objects.description: Fixed-size array type used to return sets of register IDs from cs_regs_access. Represents up to 64 16-bit register identifiers.

functions.name: cs_version
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT unsigned int CAPSTONE_API cs_version(int *major, int *minor);
functions.description: Returns the Capstone API version as a packed integer (major << 8 | minor) and optionally writes the major/minor numbers to the provided pointers. Use CS_MAKE_VERSION to compare against this return value. Pass NULL for major and/or minor if you only need the packed return value.
requirements: major may be NULL if caller does not need the major version.
minor may be NULL if caller does not need the minor version.
Return value encodes both major and minor as (major << 8 | minor).

functions.name: cs_support
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT bool CAPSTONE_API cs_support(int query);
functions.description: Queries Capstone for supported architectures or build features. Pass a CS_ARCH_* value, CS_ARCH_ALL, or special support queries like CS_SUPPORT_DIET or CS_SUPPORT_X86_REDUCE. Returns true if the architecture is supported or if the queried feature is enabled.
requirements: query must be a supported value: CS_ARCH_* (or CS_ARCH_ALL) to check architecture support, or CS_SUPPORT_DIET / CS_SUPPORT_X86_REDUCE for build features.
Returns true if the library supports the queried architecture or feature; false otherwise.

functions.name: cs_open
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT cs_err CAPSTONE_API cs_open(cs_arch arch, cs_mode mode, csh *handle);
functions.description: Initializes a Capstone disassembly handle for a given architecture and mode. Must be called before using other Capstone APIs (except cs_option with CS_OPT_MEM). On success, sets *handle to a valid handle.
requirements: arch must be a valid cs_arch (CS_ARCH_*).
mode must be a valid combination of cs_mode flags for the chosen architecture.
handle must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created handle.
Returns CS_ERR_OK on success; otherwise a cs_err code such as CS_ERR_ARCH or CS_ERR_MODE.

functions.name: cs_close
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT cs_err CAPSTONE_API cs_close(csh *handle);
functions.description: Closes a Capstone handle and releases associated cached memory. After calling, the handle is invalidated (set to 0). Must only be called when you are completely done using Capstone, including any cs_insn arrays obtained from the handle.
requirements: handle must be a non-NULL pointer to a handle previously returned by cs_open.
Must only be called when there is no further usage of Capstone APIs or any cs_insn arrays obtained from this handle; using Capstone after cs_close may crash the application.
On success, *handle is set to 0.
Returns CS_ERR_OK on success; otherwise a cs_err code.

functions.name: cs_option
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT cs_err CAPSTONE_API cs_option(csh handle, cs_opt_type type, size_t value);
functions.description: Sets runtime options on the Capstone engine such as syntax, detail mode, skipdata, mode changes, custom memory functions, mnemonic customization, and unsigned immediates printing. For CS_OPT_MEM, this can and should be called before cs_open to install custom allocators.
requirements: type must be a valid cs_opt_type (e.g., CS_OPT_SYNTAX, CS_OPT_DETAIL, CS_OPT_MODE, CS_OPT_MEM, CS_OPT_SKIPDATA, CS_OPT_SKIPDATA_SETUP, CS_OPT_MNEMONIC, CS_OPT_UNSIGNED).

value must match the expected type/value for the option (e.g., cs_opt_value for CS_OPT_SYNTAX/CS_OPT_DETAIL/CS_OPT_SKIPDATA/CS_OPT_UNSIGNED; pointer to cs_opt_mem for CS_OPT_MEM; pointer to cs_opt_skipdata for CS_OPT_SKIPDATA_SETUP; pointer to cs_opt_mnem for CS_OPT_MNEMONIC; cs_mode flags for CS_OPT_MODE).
For CS_OPT_MEM, handle may be any value and the call must occur even before cs_open to set custom memory functions.
For other option types, handle must be a valid handle returned by cs_open.
Returns CS_ERR_OK on success; otherwise a cs_err code such as CS_ERR_OPTION or CS_ERR_CSH.

functions.name: cs_errno
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT cs_err CAPSTONE_API cs_errno(csh handle);
functions.description: Returns the last error code for the given handle, similar to errno semantics. The value may change once accessed and does not persist across calls.
requirements: handle must be a handle returned by cs_open.
Return value is a cs_err (CS_ERR_*).

functions.name: cs_strerror
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT const char * CAPSTONE_API cs_strerror(cs_err code);
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing the specified cs_err error code.
requirements: code must be a valid cs_err value.
Returns a pointer to a static string describing the error code; never modifies caller memory.

functions.name: cs_disasm
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT size_t CAPSTONE_API cs_disasm(csh handle, const uint8_t *code, size_t code_size, uint64_t address, size_t count, cs_insn **insn);
functions.description: Disassembles binary code into an array of cs_insn structures. Allocates memory for the output array and stores it in *insn; the caller must free it with cs_free. If count is 0, disassembles until buffer end or an invalid instruction is encountered.
requirements: handle must be a valid handle from cs_open configured for the code’s architecture/mode.
code must point to a valid buffer of machine code bytes of length code_size.
insn must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated array; on success, must be freed with cs_free(*insn, returned_count).
address is the start address (instruction address base) for the first byte in code.
count specifies the maximum number of instructions to decode, or 0 to decode until input end or invalid instruction.
Returns the number of successfully disassembled instructions, or 0 on failure; on failure, call cs_errno(handle) for an error code.

functions.name: cs_free
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT void CAPSTONE_API cs_free(cs_insn *insn, size_t count);
functions.description: Frees memory allocated by cs_disasm (for arrays of cs_insn) or cs_malloc (for a single cs_insn).
requirements: insn must be a pointer previously returned by cs_disasm (pass the count returned by cs_disasm) or by cs_malloc (pass count=1).
count must equal the number of cs_insn structures to free (the size returned by cs_disasm), or be 1 when freeing memory from cs_malloc.

functions.name: cs_malloc
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT cs_insn * CAPSTONE_API cs_malloc(csh handle);
functions.description: Allocates memory for a single cs_insn structure suitable for use with cs_disasm_iter. Free with cs_free(insn, 1) when no longer needed.
requirements: handle must be a valid handle from cs_open.
The returned pointer must be freed with cs_free(pointer, 1).

functions.name: cs_disasm_iter
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT bool CAPSTONE_API cs_disasm_iter(csh handle, const uint8_t **code, size_t *size, uint64_t *address, cs_insn *insn);
functions.description: Iteratively disassembles one instruction at a time using a caller-provided cs_insn cache. On success, updates *code, *size, and *address to point to the next instruction in the buffer. Recommended for constrained environments and efficient iteration.
requirements: handle must be a valid handle from cs_open.
code must be a non-NULL pointer to a pointer to the current position in the input buffer; on success, *code is advanced past the decoded instruction.
size must be a non-NULL pointer to the remaining number of bytes in the buffer; on success, *size is decremented by the size of the decoded instruction.
address must be a non-NULL pointer to the current instruction address; on success, *address is advanced by the size of the decoded instruction.
insn must point to a cs_insn previously allocated by cs_malloc(handle).
Returns true on successful decoding of one instruction; false otherwise. On failure, call cs_errno(handle) for an error code.

functions.name: cs_reg_name
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT const char * CAPSTONE_API cs_reg_name(csh handle, unsigned int reg_id);
functions.description: Returns the friendly string name for a register id, or NULL if the id is invalid. Not available in diet builds where register names are not stored.
requirements: handle must be a valid handle from cs_open.
reg_id must be a valid register id for the architecture; otherwise NULL is returned.
In diet mode (cs_support(CS_SUPPORT_DIET) == true), this API is irrelevant and may not return names.

functions.name: cs_insn_name
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT const char * CAPSTONE_API cs_insn_name(csh handle, unsigned int insn_id);
functions.description: Returns the friendly mnemonic name for an instruction id, or NULL if the id is invalid. Not available in diet builds where instruction names are not stored.
requirements: handle must be a valid handle from cs_open.
insn_id must be a valid instruction id for the architecture; otherwise NULL is returned.
In diet mode (cs_support(CS_SUPPORT_DIET) == true), this API is irrelevant and may not return names.

functions.name: cs_group_name
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT const char * CAPSTONE_API cs_group_name(csh handle, unsigned int group_id);
functions.description: Returns the friendly name for an instruction group id, or NULL if the id is invalid. Not available in diet builds where group names are not stored.
requirements: handle must be a valid handle from cs_open.
group_id must be a valid group id; otherwise NULL is returned.
In diet mode (cs_support(CS_SUPPORT_DIET) == true), this API is irrelevant and may not return names.

functions.name: cs_insn_group
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT bool CAPSTONE_API cs_insn_group(csh handle, const cs_insn *insn, unsigned int group_id);
functions.description: Checks whether a disassembled instruction belongs to a specified group by comparing against insn->groups. Valid only when detail mode is ON; irrelevant in diet builds that don't update groups.
requirements: handle must be a valid handle from cs_open.
insn must be a valid pointer to a cs_insn obtained from cs_disasm/cs_disasm_iter.
Detail option must be enabled (cs_option(handle, CS_OPT_DETAIL, CS_OPT_ON)); otherwise this API is invalid.
In diet mode, this API is irrelevant because the engine does not update the groups array.
Returns true if the instruction belongs to the group; false otherwise.

functions.name: cs_reg_read
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT bool CAPSTONE_API cs_reg_read(csh handle, const cs_insn *insn, unsigned int reg_id);
functions.description: Checks whether a disassembled instruction implicitly reads the specified register by searching insn->regs_read. Valid only when detail mode is ON; irrelevant in diet builds that don't update regs_read.
requirements: handle must be a valid handle from cs_open.
insn must be a valid pointer to a cs_insn obtained from cs_disasm/cs_disasm_iter.
reg_id must be a register id for the architecture.
Detail option must be enabled (cs_option(handle, CS_OPT_DETAIL, CS_OPT_ON)); otherwise this API is invalid.
In diet mode, this API is irrelevant because the engine does not update regs_read.
Returns true if the instruction implicitly reads reg_id; false otherwise.

functions.name: cs_reg_write
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT bool CAPSTONE_API cs_reg_write(csh handle, const cs_insn *insn, unsigned int reg_id);
functions.description: Checks whether a disassembled instruction implicitly writes the specified register by searching insn->regs_write. Valid only when detail mode is ON; irrelevant in diet builds that don't update regs_write.
requirements: handle must be a valid handle from cs_open.
insn must be a valid pointer to a cs_insn obtained from cs_disasm/cs_disasm_iter.
reg_id must be a register id for the architecture.
Detail option must be enabled (cs_option(handle, CS_OPT_DETAIL, CS_OPT_ON)); otherwise this API is invalid.
In diet mode, this API is irrelevant because the engine does not update regs_write.
Returns true if the instruction implicitly writes reg_id; false otherwise.

functions.name: cs_op_count
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT int CAPSTONE_API cs_op_count(csh handle, const cs_insn *insn, unsigned int op_type);
functions.description: Counts the number of operands of a particular type in a disassembled instruction. Valid only when detail mode is ON.
requirements: handle must be a valid handle from cs_open.
insn must be a valid pointer to a cs_insn obtained from cs_disasm/cs_disasm_iter.
op_type must be a valid operand type for the architecture (see arch-specific headers).
Detail option must be enabled (cs_option(handle, CS_OPT_DETAIL, CS_OPT_ON)); otherwise returns -1 on failure.
Returns the count on success, or -1 on failure.

functions.name: cs_op_index
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT int CAPSTONE_API cs_op_index(csh handle, const cs_insn *insn, unsigned int op_type, unsigned int position);
functions.description: Returns the index within the architecture-specific operands array of the nth operand (1-based) of the specified type. Valid only when detail mode is ON.
requirements: handle must be a valid handle from cs_open.
insn must be a valid pointer to a cs_insn obtained from cs_disasm/cs_disasm_iter.
op_type must be a valid operand type for the architecture (see arch-specific headers).
position must be in the range [1, cs_op_count(handle, insn, op_type)].
Detail option must be enabled (cs_option(handle, CS_OPT_DETAIL, CS_OPT_ON)); otherwise returns -1 on failure.
Returns the operand index on success, or -1 on failure.

functions.name: cs_regs_access
functions.signature: CAPSTONE_EXPORT cs_err CAPSTONE_API cs_regs_access(csh handle, const cs_insn *insn, cs_regs regs_read, uint8_t *regs_read_count, cs_regs regs_write, uint8_t *regs_write_count);
functions.description: Retrieves all registers read and written by a disassembled instruction, both explicitly and implicitly. Fills the provided arrays and counts. Not available in diet builds that do not store register information.
requirements: handle must be a valid handle from cs_open.
insn must be a valid pointer to a cs_insn returned by cs_disasm/cs_disasm_iter.
regs_read must be a writable cs_regs array to receive read registers.
regs_read_count must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the count of read registers.
regs_write must be a writable cs_regs array to receive written registers.
regs_write_count must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the count of written registers.
In diet mode, this API is irrelevant because the engine does not store registers and may fail with CS_ERR_DIET.
Returns CS_ERR_OK on success; otherwise a cs_err code.

data_types.description: An arbitrary sequence of bytes interpreted as machine code for the architecture/mode configured in the disassembly handle. The data is not text; it is a binary buffer containing instruction opcodes that cs_disasm/cs_disasm_iter will attempt to decode. Any byte values (0x00–0xFF) are valid and length can vary.

import random
from typing import List

# This generator produces raw machine-code byte buffers that are likely valid
# for several architectures Capstone supports. We include hand-crafted opcode
# sequences for common ISAs and randomly concatenate a few sequences to build
# a buffer. The data is binary (not text) and limited to <=4096 bytes.
#
# Architectures covered with short, valid encodings:
# - x86 (16/32/64): NOP sleds, MOV/ADD/SUB/RET/CALL/JMP, prefix mixes
# - ARM (A32/Thumb): BX LR, MOV, ADD, B, BL
# - ARM64 (AArch64): NOP, RET, MOVZ/MOVK, ADD/SUB immediate, B/BL
# - MIPS: NOP, J, JAL, ADDI, ORI
# - RISCV: NOP, ADDI, JAL, JALR, AUIPC
# - PPC: NOP variant, B, BL, ADDI
# - SPARC: NOP, BA, CALL
# - 68K: NOP, RTS, BRA
# - WASM: simple opcodes sequence (valid single-byte operators)
# - BPF: classic and eBPF small sequences
#
# We keep each snippet valid for its ISA and then mix snippets from one chosen
# ISA per buffer to maximize chance of successful disassembly under the fuzzer's
# current handle/mode.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Helper to convert hex string (with spaces) to bytes
_def = lambda s: bytes(int(b, 16) for b in s.strip().split())

# Snippet libraries per architecture. Each is a list[bytes].
SNIPPETS = {
    "x86": [
        _def("90"),                            # NOP
        _def("C3"),                            # RET
        _def("CC"),                            # INT3
        _def("55 48 89 E5"),                  # push rbp; mov rbp,rsp
        _def("48 31 C0 C3"),                  # xor rax,rax; ret
        _def("B8 34 12 00 00 C3"),            # mov eax,0x1234; ret
        _def("E8 00 00 00 00"),               # call rel32 (next instr)
        _def("EB 00"),                        # jmp short +0
        _def("F3 90"),                        # pause (rep nop)
        _def("66 90"),                        # xchg ax,ax (nop-like)
        _def("48 83 EC 10 48 83 C4 10 C3"),   # sub rsp,16; add rsp,16; ret
        _def("0F 1F 00"),                     # 3-byte NOP
        _def("64 65 2E F3 90"),               # prefix soup + nop
        _def("48 FF C0"),                     # inc rax
        _def("48 89 D8"),                     # mov rax, rbx
    ],
    "arm": [
        _def("00 F0 20 E3"),                  # nop (mov r0, r0) A32
        _def("1E FF 2F E1"),                  # bx lr A32
        _def("04 00 A0 E1"),                  # mov r0, r4 A32
        _def("00 10 81 E2"),                  # add r1, r1, #0
        _def("FE FF FF EA"),                  # b . (infinite)
        # Thumb/Thumb-2 (placed standalone so either mode may pick some)
        _def("70 47"),                        # bx lr (Thumb)
        _def("00 BF"),                        # nop (Thumb)
        _def("00 B5 00 BD"),                  # push {lr}; pop {pc} (Thumb)
        _def("00 F0 00 F8"),                  # bl to next (Thumb-2)
    ],
    "arm64": [
        _def("1F 20 03 D5"),                  # nop
        _def("C0 03 5F D6"),                  # ret
        _def("20 00 80 D2"),                  # mov x0,#1 (movz x0, #1)
        _def("00 00 80 D2 C0 03 5F D6"),      # movz x0,#0 ; ret
        _def("00 04 00 11"),                  # add w0,w0,#1
        _def("00 00 00 14"),                  # b .
        _def("00 00 00 94"),                  # bl .
        _def("E1 0B 80 D2 01 10 A0 F2"),      # mov x1,#0x5F (movz/movk)
    ],
    "mips": [
        _def("00 00 00 00"),                  # nop
        _def("08 00 E0 03"),                  # jr ra
        _def("25 08 00 00"),                  # or a0,zero,zero
        _def("0C 00 00 00"),                  # jal 0
        _def("20 00 08 24"),                  # addiu t0,zero,0x20
        _def("0A 00 00 10"),                  # beqz zero, +0x28 (likely skip)
    ],
    "riscv": [
        _def("13 00 00 00"),                  # nop (addi x0,x0,0)
        _def("93 00 10 00"),                  # addi x1,x0,1
        _def("EF 00 00 00"),                  # jal x0,0
        _def("67 80 00 00"),                  # jalr x0,0(x1)
        _def("17 05 00 00"),                  # auipc x10,0
    ],
    "ppc": [
        _def("60 00 00 00"),                  # ori r0,r0,0 (nop-like)
        _def("4E 80 00 20"),                  # blr
        _def("48 00 00 00"),                  # b 0
        _def("4B FF FF FC"),                  # b -4 (loop)
        _def("38 60 00 00"),                  # li r3,0 (addi r3,r0,0)
    ],
    "sparc": [
        _def("01 00 00 00"),                  # nop
        _def("81 C3 E0 08"),                  # retl
        _def("10 BF FF FF"),                  # ba .-4 (loop)
        _def("40 00 00 00"),                  # call 0
    ],
    "m68k": [
        _def("4E 71"),                        # nop
        _def("4E 75"),                        # rts
        _def("60 00 00 00"),                  # bra 0 (long)
        _def("70 00"),                        # moveq #0,d0
    ],
    "wasm": [
        # Simple, valid opcode bytes without length prefixes; Capstone can decode opcodes.
        _def("00"),                           # unreachable
        _def("01"),                           # nop
        _def("0B"),                           # end
        _def("0C 00"),                        # br 0
        _def("41 00"),                        # i32.const 0
        _def("6A"),                           # i32.add
    ],
    "bpf": [
        # Classic BPF 8-byte insns: code(1) jt(1) jf(1) k(4) -> represent as bytes
        # Use simple return statements; Capstone can parse classic and eBPF when mode set.
        # classic: RET K 0 -> 0x06 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
        _def("06 00 00 00 00 00 00 00"),
        # classic: RET K 0xFFFFFFFF
        _def("06 00 00 FF FF FF FF 00"),
        # eBPF 8-byte encoding examples: nop and exit-like sequences
        _def("95 00 00 00 00 00 00 00"),      # exit
        _def("B7 00 00 00 2A 00 00 00"),      # mov r0,42
        _def("95 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 B7 00 00 00 2A 00 00 00 95 00 00 00 00 00 00 00"),
    ],
}

ARCH_KEYS: List[str] = list(SNIPPETS.keys())

def _build_for_arch(rng: random.Random, arch: str, target_size: int) -> bytes:
    seqs = SNIPPETS[arch]
    out = bytearray()
    # Choose between 1 and up to N snippets to approach target_size
    while len(out) < target_size:
        chunk = rng.choice(seqs)
        # Occasionally repeat-friendly instructions (like nops) to pad
        reps = 1
        if len(chunk) <= 2:
            reps = rng.randint(1, min(32, max(1, (target_size - len(out)) // max(1, len(chunk)))))
        for _ in range(reps):
            out += chunk
            if len(out) >= target_size:
                break
        # Sometimes insert short alignment padding
        if rng.random() < 0.2 and len(out) + 4 <= target_size:
            if arch in ("x86", "arm64", "arm"):
                out += b"\x90" * rng.randint(1, 4)  # x86 nop; harmless elsewhere too
            else:
                out += b"\x00" * rng.randint(1, 4)
    return bytes(out[:target_size])

def _choose_target_size(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Favor small to medium buffers, with occasional larger ones up to 512 (per stub cap)
    # but allow up to 1024 to be safe; the stub will truncate to its own max.
    buckets = [8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 384, 512]
    w = [10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 8, 6, 4]
    size = rng.choices(buckets, weights=w, k=1)[0]
    # Small jitter
    jitter = rng.randint(0, size // 8)
    return min(MAX_SIZE, size + jitter)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    arch = rng.choice(ARCH_KEYS)
    target_size = _choose_target_size(rng)

    # Sometimes bias specific ISA depending on seed aspects to diversify
    if seed % 7 == 0:
        arch = "x86"
    elif seed % 11 == 0:
        arch = "arm64"
    elif seed % 13 == 0:
        arch = "riscv"

    buf = _build_for_arch(rng, arch, target_size)

    # Occasionally prepend small prologue or address-sensitive bytes
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and len(buf) < MAX_SIZE:
        if arch == "x86":
            pro = _def("55 48 89 E5")
        elif arch == "arm64":
            pro = _def("1F 20 03 D5")  # nop
        elif arch == "arm":
            pro = _def("00 BF")        # thumb nop (still fine as bytes)
        else:
            pro = b"\x00\x00"
        buf = (pro + buf)[:MAX_SIZE]

    return buf
